issue.body: fix(ivy): narrow `NgIf` context variables in template type checker When the `NgIf` directive is used in a template, its context variables can be used to capture the bound value. This is typically used together with a pipe or function call, where the resulting value is captured in a context variable. There's two syntax forms available: 1. Binding to `NgIfContext.ngIf` using the `as` syntax: ```html {{user.name}} ``` 2. Binding to `NgIfContext.$implicit` using the `let` syntax: ```html {{user.name}} ``` Because of the semantics of `ngIf`, it is known that the captured context variable is non-nullable, however the template type checker would not consider them as such and still report errors when `strictNullTypes` is enabled. This commit updates `NgIf`'s context guard to make the types of the context variables non-nullable, avoiding the issue. Fixes #34572

issue.body:
# 🐞 bug report

### Affected Package
@angular/language-service


### Is this a regression?

No.


### Description

Language service is not working correctly with `ngIf` and `strictNullChecks`.

There is a [documentation](https://angular.io/guide/template-syntax#the-non-null-assertion-operator---) about this exact thing, but it makes no sense because of the following:

1. **Following TypeScript code is OK with full `strict` mode enabled**

```typescript
public obj?: { val: string };

if (this.obj) {
  console.log(this.obj.val); // IT'S ALL GOOD
}
```

2. **The same logic in Angular template throws an error trough language service:**

```html
<ng-container *ngIf="obj">{{ obj.val }}</ng-container>
```

This really makes no sense, and the official solution is to add `!` after `obj`, like `{{ obj!.val }}` which feels more like a workaround.

I did as well found out that creating a variable in ngIf directive will prevent the error from appearing, therefore it is inconsistent as well:

```html
<ng-container *ngIf="obj; let obj">{{ obj.val }}</ng-container>
```

## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction

In any latest Angular project, that is using `@angular/language-service` apply code snippets from the description.

## 🔥 Exception or Error

`[Angular] The expression might be null`

## 🌍  Your Environment

**Angular Version:**

```
Angular CLI: 7.2.1
Node: 10.15.0
OS: darwin x64
Angular: 7.2.0
... animations, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms
... http, language-service, platform-browser
... platform-browser-dynamic, router
```

**Anything else relevant?**

If required I can create a repository with the code snippets. I didn't do so because it should be easy to reproduce. If I am wrong, please let me know and I will provide the repo.

{{ test.a }} {{ test.q }} {{ test.a.w }}

{{ test.a }} {{ test.q }} {{ test.a.w }}
